item.title: Senate committee votes to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress
item.description: The Senate Homeland Security Committee voted to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress over his refusal to answer questions during testimony before the committee last week.

item.title: FDA approves Moderna's mRNA flu vaccine after initial pushback
item.description: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has approved a new seasonal flu vaccine from Moderna that uses mRNA technology, the drugmaker announced.

item.title: Can debt collectors re-age an old debt? 5 things to know now
item.description: While debt collectors have broad authority to pursue unpaid balances, there are important limits to know.

item.title: What will Trump's Air Force One jet be used for after his term ends?
item.description: President Trump initially said his Qatari-gifted Air Force One would be put in his presidential library after his second term ends, but his son Eric says otherwise. Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: More adults are living with their parents now than during the pandemic. Here's why.
item.description: A record number of U.S. adults are moving back in with their parents. Dr. Gail Saltz, a psychiatrist at NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital and Weill-Cornell Medical College, and CBS News business analyst Jill Schlesinger explain what's behind the trend, and how to make it work.

item.title: Watch live trial: Lindsay Clancy sobs as jury is shown autopsy photos
item.description: The Lindsay Clancy trial continues on Day 8 of testimony with a Massachusetts medical examiner taking the stand.

item.title: Here's what to know about the new mRNA flu vaccine
item.description: The FDA has approved a new flu vaccine that uses mRNA technology. Dr. Céline Gounder reports.

item.title: Iran, Oman deal on Strait of Hormuz getting close, Tehran says
item.description: Iran and Oman are close to agreeing on new arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz, but not for a full reopening of the vital waterway, Iran's state news agency says.

item.title: What to expect ahead of the July jobs report after data shows little movement
item.description: The Bureau of Labor Statistics will release its July jobs report on Friday, August 7. CBS News business analyst Jill Schlesinger has more on what to expect. (Sponsored by AT&T Business)

item.title: Investment tips for the booming stock market
item.description: Jill Schlesinger joins "CBS Mornings" to share investment tips amid a booming stock market.

item.title: Record number of adults moving back in with their parents as cost of living soars
item.description: With wages stagnant, inflation up, and the cost of living increasing, more American adults are seeing their parents as potential roommates as they look to save cash. CBS MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo has more.

item.title: What this year's "El Niño" means for hurricane season and global weather
item.description: This year's unusually intense El Niño pattern could have an immense impact on global weather. Meteorologist Rob Marciano explains.

item.title: Senate committee votes to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress after bombastic COVID hearing
item.description: The Republican-led Senate Homeland Security Committee voted to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress after he invoked the Fifth Amendment during a Senate hearing on the origins of COVID-19. CBS News' Taurean Small reports.

item.title: Man says he's rethinking Trump vote after his fiancee was arrested by ICE in airport
item.description: ICE detentions were at a Trump-era high in July, with many detainees picked up at airports. A man told Camilo Montoya-Galvez he's rethinking his vote for President Trump following his fiancée's arrest in an airport.

item.title: Minnesota Chipotle burrito bowl meal led to sepsis hospitalization, lawsuit says
item.description: A Minnesota woman says she fainted, spiked a 102-degree fever, and was hospitalized with sepsis three days after eating a chicken burrito bowl at a Chipotle in Roseville, and genetic testing connected her case to a multistate outbreak, according to a lawsuit filed Tuesday.

item.title: Hungary's only nuclear plant on brink of shutdown as Danube River dries up
item.description: Hungary's only nuclear plant, which relies on water from the Danube River, could be forced to close amid a drought. CBS News' Ramy Inocencio reports.

item.title: Cyberattacks possibly linked to Iran threatened water systems in a dozen states, sources say
item.description: U.S. officials suspect Iran-backed hackers may be behind cyberattacks that have been reported in at least 12 states. CBS News homeland security correspondent Nicole Sganga has more details.

item.title: At least 12 states report cyberattacks on water systems possibly linked to Iran
item.description: Cyberattacks on U.S. water systems that officials suspect may be linked to Iran-backed hackers have been reported in at least a dozen states, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News.

item.title: What to know about U.S. water systems hacks that could be linked to Iran
item.description: U.S. officials are investigating hacks into the country's water systems that could be linked to Iran. Nicole Sganga has more.

item.title: Deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz with Oman is getting close, Iran says
item.description: Oman and Iran are hammering out the final details of a deal to reopen and jointly manage the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iran's foreign minister. BBC News' Jon Donnison reports.

item.title: FAA, NTSB investigating why passenger plane took off near Marine One
item.description: A commercial aircraft was allowed to take off in Washington, D.C., on Tuesday afternoon despite Marine One flying nearby. The FAA and NTSB are investigating. Kris Van Cleave has the latest.

item.title: Washington, California wildfires spark air quality concerns
item.description: Wildfires near Spokane, Washington, have destroyed more than 800 buildings, and have sparked major air quality concerns. Meanwhile, blazes near Sacramento, California, threaten hundreds of homes. Rob Marciano reports.

item.title: Republicans accuse Michigan's El-Sayed of being "too extreme" after Senate primary win
item.description: Republicans are bracing for November's midterm elections after Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed narrowly beat Haley Stevens in the Democratic Senate primary on Tuesday. Caitlin Huey-Burns has the latest.

item.title: Chipotle removes jalapeños linked to Minnesota salmonella outbreak
item.description: The restaurant chain said it pulled the peppers and replaced them with product from another grower amid a food-poisoning probe.

item.title: U.S. hit with more foodborne illnesses as Chipotle, Qdoba remove salmonella-linked jalapeños
item.description: The U.S. has been hit with another foodborne illness outbreak, as Chipotle, Qdoba and other restaurants pull jalapeños linked to salmonella. Meanwhile, officials are still struggling with a cyclosporiasis outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce. Shanelle Kaul has more.

item.title: Trump voter pleads for fiancée's release after ICE arrest: "They're destroying families"
item.description: "They are picking up law-abiding citizens. They're destroying families, jobs," said a Texas man who regrets his vote for President Trump after his fiancée, an immigrant from Venezuela, was detained by ICE.

item.title: AI models are behaving unexpectedly. Experts warn of a "bumpy road" ahead.
item.description: AI models are engaging in unauthorized actions — in the most recent case, creating fake identities and attempting to persuade real people to approve malicious code.

item.title: Meta says its AI model breached a third-party company during testing
item.description: Tech giant Meta revealed Wednesday that one of its artificial intelligence models hacked another organization during testing, the third time in recent weeks that an AI model has improperly accessed a third-party company.

item.title: Qdoba removes jalapeños as salmonella outbreak spreads to 27 states
item.description: At least 345 people — the majority in Colorado and Minnesota — have been sickened by a salmonella outbreak, according to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

item.title: Cyclospora outbreak tied to lettuce now linked to 15 states, CDC says
item.description: Cyclospora cases have been reported in at least 47 states total this year, and investigators have continued to probe how many could be linked to a common contaminated source.
